plan.hypothesis: Frequency-sensitive transition deviance improves reordered-tool detection compared with transition-presence features.
plan.design_status: Fixed before generating or scoring the fresh test batches; motivated by the previously inspected v2 sequence-family failure.

sequence_model.name: markov_deviance
sequence_model.unknown_tool: reserved bucket within fitted actor vocabulary
sequence_model.unknown_actor: explicit error; no pooling across tenants or actors
sequence_model.score: 2 times mean conditional transition log likelihood ratio: empirical session next-tool probabilities versus smoothed training next-tool probabilities

plan.primary_comparison: fresh_sequence calibrated and capped recall against rules, robust_distance and isolation_forest on identical sessions

order_control.method: one within-session random tool permutation, leaving timestamps, outcomes and tool multisets intact; score diagnostic only, not a new labeled attack test

plan.promotion_policy: Report all predeclared batches and comparators; do not tune, replace the reference detector or choose seeds after seeing fresh test results.
limitations: Fresh instances of an already inspected synthetic family, not a blind family holdout.
Length-normalized empirical transition deviance retains finite-sample and tool-composition effects.
First-order transitions cannot distinguish sequences sharing transition counts.
Training labels remain unused despite contamination; no production efficacy claim.
